Phoney War: Initial period of low activity in World War II.
This Macedonian Greek general, one of Alexander the Great's most trusted companions, retrieved his leader's body after his death and founded a new ruling dynasty in Egypt — who is he?
Ptolemy I Soter: Pharaoh of Egypt from 305 to 282 BC.
Taking office in December 1983, this Argentine lawyer and social democrat was the first democratically elected president after the country's military 'National Reorganization Process' — who was he?
Raúl Alfonsín: President of Argentina from 1983 to 1989.
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.
In 2023 this German politician walked out of The Left to found a Eurosceptic populist party bearing her own name — which firebrand was she?

Depicted in reliefs at Ramesses III's mortuary temple, this mysterious maritime confederation was long blamed for Late Bronze Age raids on Egypt around 1200 BC, though scholars now see them more as a symptom of the era's collapse than its cause. Who were they?
Sea Peoples: Purported ancient tribal confederation of the Late Bronze Age.
Born Farid Khan, this 16th-century ruler founded an empire after defeating the Mughals and made Delhi his capital, earning the title 'the Just King' — who is he?
Sher Shah Suri: Sultan of Hindustan from 1540 to 1545.
Succeeding his father David as king of ancient Israel, this biblical ruler's wealth and foreign wives allegedly introduced idolatry, sowing the seeds for the kingdom's later split. Who is he?
Solomon: Biblical monarch of ancient Israel. The successor of his father David, he is described as the penultimate ruler of all Twelve Tribes of Israel under a united Israel and Judah.
Commonly called "SBY," this retired general was only the second military man after Suharto to become Indonesia's president, serving two terms from 2004 — who is he?

Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono: President of Indonesia from 2004 to 2014. Yudhoyono won the 2004 presidential election—the first direct presidential election in Indonesia, defeating incumbent President Megawati Sukarnoputri.
In Greek mythology, this minor deity personified death itself, and was known to the Romans as Mors or Letum — who is he?
Thanatos: Ancient Greek personification of death.

Nicknamed 'The Tiger of Malaya' after conquering the peninsula and a nearby island stronghold in just 70 days, this WWII Japanese general later held out on Luzon until his country's surrender in 1945 — who is he?
Tomoyuki Yamashita: Japanese officer and war criminal (1885–1946)
In Norse belief, these female figures guide fallen warriors to Odin's hall, sometimes shown accompanied by ravens, swans, or wolves — what are they called?
This American divorcée's romance with Britain's king forced his abdication in 1936 rather than let her become queen — who was she?
Wallis Simpson: Wife of Prince Edward, Duke of Windsor (1896–1986)

One of three brothers with distinguished military careers, this British general rose to Commander-in-Chief, America, during the War of Independence after famously scaling the cliffs at Quebec in 1759. Who was he?
William Howe, 5th Viscount Howe: British Army officer and politician (1729–1814)

Rooted in pre-Islamic Kurdish tradition and shaped by Sufi influence, this monotheistic faith reveres a 'Peacock Angel' as chief among seven angels tasked with guarding the world — which religion is it?
The eldest child of Alfred the Great, this Anglo-Saxon noblewoman ruled the Mercians in her own right from 911 until her death in 918 — who was she?
Æthelflæd: Ruler of Mercia in England from 911 to 918.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (born 1847) is the earliest of the four. Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 – March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest release?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Jan Baptist van Helmont is a chemist.
What is the atomic number of Carbon?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
In what year was J. Robert Oppenheimer born?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year was Arthur Conan Doyle born?
Arthur Conan Doyle: Sir Arthur Ignatius Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 – 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
In what year was José M. Hernández born?
José M. Hernández: José Moreno Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
In what year did Jean Tatlock die?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year did Anton Chekhov die?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation
Ondansetron: Pfizer. It is also effective for treating gastroenteritis.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
Often caused by misaligned or unevenly focused eyes in early childhood, this is the most common cause of single-eye vision loss in kids and young adults, nicknamed 'lazy eye' — what condition is it?
Amblyopia is a disorder of sight in which the brain fails to fully process input from one eye and over time favors the other eye.
This lustrous grey metalloid, found mainly in the mineral stibnite, was historically powdered for use as a cosmetic known by its Arabic name, kohl. What element is it?
Antimony is a chemical element with the symbol Sb (from Latin stibium) and atomic number 51.

This lung condition — the partial collapse of alveoli that reduces gas exchange, usually in just one lung — is a very common finding on chest X-rays, though it's technically distinct from a fluid-filled lung or a full pneumothorax — what is it?
Atelectasis is the partial collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced or absent gas exchange, more specifically the collapse of alveoli.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
This family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, sheep, and goats across 143 living species — name the family?
Bovidae is the biological family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals that includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, and goat-antelopes such as sheep and goats.
Originating from the now-discredited caloric theory of heat, this unit of energy is defined as the amount of heat needed to raise one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius — name the unit?
Calorie is a unit of energy that originated from the caloric theory of heat.
Discovered in 1801 by Giuseppe Piazzi and initially hailed as a new planet, this object in the main asteroid belt is now the only recognized dwarf planet orbiting within Neptune's path — what is it?
Ceres (dwarf planet) is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
After serving as dean of Harvard's Faculty of Arts and Sciences, this political scientist became the university's 30th president in July 2023 — who is she?
Claudine Gay (born August 4, 1970) is an American political scientist who is the Wilbur A. Cowett Professor of Government and of African and African-American Studies at Harvard University.
This transparent dome covering the iris and pupil provides about two-thirds of the eye's total focusing power and can be reshaped via LASIK surgery — what is it?
Cornea is the transparent front part of the eye which covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
What unit of time, roughly 24 hours long, marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun and drives the circadian rhythms of most living things?
Day is the time period of a full rotation of the Earth with respect to the Sun.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
Confirming Maxwell's theoretical predictions, this 19th-century German physicist proved that electromagnetic waves actually exist — who is he?

Heinrich Hertz (hurts; 22 February 1857 - 1 January 1894) was a German physicist who first conclusively proved the existence of the electromagnetic waves proposed by James Clerk Maxwell's equations of electromagnetism.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This analytical framework, which arose partly in reaction to both white feminism and the male-dominated Black liberation movement, examines how overlapping social identities create unique combinations of discrimination and privilege — name the concept?
Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege.
Holder of 128 firearm patents, this American engineer invented the telescoping bolt that made compact autoloading pistols possible — who is he?

John Browning (January 23, 1855 - November 26, 1926) was an American firearm designer who developed many varieties of military and civilian firearms, cartridges, and gun mechanisms, many of which are still in use around the world.
Named after the American endocrinologist who identified it in the 1940s, this chromosome anomaly, also called 47,XXY, typically affects phenotypic males with infertility. What condition is it?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
This big-cat hybrid, born of a male lion and a female tiger, is the largest of all living cats, growing larger than either parent and enjoying a swim. What animal is it?
Liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).

Developed by MathWorks, this proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment is built around matrix manipulation, and pairs with an add-on called Simulink for graphical simulation and model-based design. What software is this?
MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.

Designed as both fighter and ground-attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation), this all-weather supersonic, carrier-capable twin-engined jet was derived from the YF-17 and developed for the Navy. What aircraft is this?

McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet is an all-weather supersonic, twin-engined, carrier-capable, multirole combat aircraft, designed as both a fighter and ground attack aircraft (hence the F/A designation).

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.

Native to the Horn of Africa and nicknamed the 'sand puppy,' this burrowing rodent is the only mammal that's a cold-blooded thermoconformer — and lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen. What is it?
Naked mole-rat (Heterocephalus glaber), also known as the sand puppy, is a burrowing rodent native to the Horn of Africa and parts of Kenya, notably in Somali regions.
What organic molecule, composed of a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, serves as the basic building block of both DNA and RNA?
Nucleotide are organic molecules composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate.
This rare silvery-white metal, discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, is part of the six-element platinum group and has the lowest melting point among them. What element is it?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
This class of compounds is defined by a direct single bond between two oxygen atoms, denoted R−O−O−R — what are they called?
Peroxide are a group of molecules with the structure ROOR, where each R represents a radical (a portion of a complete molecule; not a free radical) and the O's are single oxygen atoms.
In Aristotle's day this kingdom included algae and fungi, but modern definitions have narrowed it to chiefly photosynthetic, mostly multicellular organisms — what is it?
Plant are the eukaryotic organisms that constitute the kingdom Plantae.

This endogenous steroid sex hormone plays a central role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development, and also serves as a key metabolic intermediate for producing other steroid hormones — name the hormone?
Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
Bitter-tasting and rich in vitamin K, this Mediterranean vegetable with edible buds resembling broccoli is also known as broccoli rabe — what is it?
Rapini (broccoli rabe or raab; RAHB) is a green cruciferous vegetable, with the leaves, buds, and stems all being edible; the buds somewhat resemble broccoli.
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
First described in 1779, which large African raptor stands over four feet tall on stilt-like legs and is grouped in its own family, Sagittariidae?
Secretarybird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa.
Once placed alone in the genus Uncia before phylogenetics moved it into Panthera, this high-altitude cat ranges across the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas — what is it?
Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.
This muscular, hollow organ in the upper digestive tract handles the gastric phase of digestion, and gives us the medical prefix 'gastric' from its Ancient Greek name — name the organ?
Stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.

This chalcogen element, chemically similar to selenium and sulfur, is far more abundant in the universe than on Earth because its hydride escaped into space during our planet's formation — which element?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.

First identified in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist analyzing a mineral he dubbed 'brown lead,' this hard, silvery-grey transition metal carries atomic number 23 and chemical symbol V — what's the element?
Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
Caused by a mutation in the ATP7B gene, this inherited condition lets copper build up in the liver and brain, leading to tremors, personality changes, and yellowing skin — which condition?
Wilson's disease (also called hepatolenticular degeneration) is a genetic disorder characterized by the excess build-up of copper in the body.
This painful collection of pus built up within body tissue often causes redness, warmth, and swelling, and includes boils and carbuncles as common types — what is it called?
Abscess: Localized collection of pus in body tissue. An abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
This wide-body twinjet shares its wing and much of its structure with the four-engined A340, and it first carried passengers for Air Inter in January 1994 — which aircraft is it?
Native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa, this flowering plant lent its name — and originally its root — to a fluffy campfire treat, and is used in herbal medicine — which plant?
Its name comes from Latin words meaning 'to strangle' and 'chest,' and it describes pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle — what is this condition called?
Angina: Chest discomfort due to disorder of the heart muscles.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?

Related to the tufted and horned members of its family found in the Pacific, this seabird breeds from Iceland to Newfoundland and dives underwater to catch zooplankton, small fish and crabs — which auk is this?
Atlantic puffin: Species of seabird. The Atlantic puffin (Fratercula arctica), also known as the common puffin, is a species of seabird in the auk family.

This facial hair — most common among adult men, though it can also appear in women with a condition called hirsutism — has symbolized everything from wisdom and virility to poor hygiene across different cultures — what is it?
Beard: Hair on the chin, lower face and neck.
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.
Once common as the refrigerant "Freon," these carbon-chlorine-fluorine compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for chewing through the ozone layer — what are they?
Home to jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones, this phylum of aquatic invertebrates is defined by specialized stinging cells used to capture prey — what is it?
Cnidaria: Aquatic animal phylum having cnidocytes.

This physician was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 after inadvertently overdosing his famous patient with the anesthetic propofol, which he had been improperly using as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray: American physician and convicted felon (born 1953)
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
Dubbed 'the father of immunology,' this English physician created the world's first vaccine using cowpox to fight a disease that once killed up to a fifth of city dwellers — who is he?
Native to French Polynesia but nicknamed 'devil's ivy' for staying green even in the dark, this hardy houseplant has become an invasive nuisance worldwide — what's its scientific name?

Famous for the male's song delivered while hovering 50 to 100 metres above open farmland, this streaked greyish-brown bird has been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark: Species of bird. The Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
Likely domesticated from the European polecat, with which it can still interbreed to produce hybrids, this slender mustelid averages about 50 centimeters long — what is it?
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Bred at a Scottish estate by crossing a flat-coated gun dog with Tweed Water Spaniels, this gentle, honey-coated working dog was recognized by the Kennel Club in 1913 — which breed?
Golden Retriever: Scottish breed of dog. It is characterised by a gentle and affectionate nature and a striking golden coat.
Published in 1931 by an Austrian logician, these two results proved that any consistent axiom system for arithmetic will always contain true statements it cannot prove — what are they called?
Gödel's incompleteness theorems: Limitative results in mathematical logic.

This French mathematician reinvented what it means to find the area under a curve, publishing his sweeping new theory of integration in a 1902 dissertation titled "Integral, length, area." Who was he?
Strongly associated with human habitation and now the most widely distributed wild bird on Earth thanks to introductions across multiple continents, this small brown-and-black bird is which species?
House sparrow: Species of bird. The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world.

Once diagnosed almost exclusively in women during the 19th century and studied intensely by Sigmund Freud and Jean-Martin Charcot, this term for 'ungovernable emotional excess' is no longer accepted as a medical diagnosis. What is it called?
Hysteria: Excess, ungovernable emotion. Hysteria is a term used to mean ungovernable emotional excess and can refer to a temporary state of mind or emotion.

He won the 1944 Nobel Prize for his resonance method of recording the magnetic properties of atomic nuclei, and was among the first Americans to work on the cavity magnetron behind radar and microwave ovens — which physicist?

A former Chicago options trader with finance degrees but no PhD, this entrepreneur co-founded a dot-com company whose peer-reviewed project evolved into the world's largest free encyclopedia — who is he?

Caused by a herpesvirus and linked to weakened immunity such as HIV/AIDS, this cancer produces purple skin lesions and disproportionately affects older Mediterranean men in its 'classic' form — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma: Cancer of the skin, integumentary lymph nodes, or other organs.
About 1.5 metres long and beginning at the cecum via the ileocecal valve, this final section of the human gut absorbs water and salt before waste reaches the rectum — what part of the body is it?
Large intestine: Last part of the digestive system in vertebrates.
Sometimes called the paleomammalian cortex, this set of brain structures — including the amygdala — governs emotion, motivation, and long-term memory — what is it called?
Limbic system: Set of brain structures involved in emotion and motivation. Its various components support a variety of functions including emotion, behavior, long-term memory, and olfaction.

This German fluid dynamicist built the mathematical foundations of subsonic aerodynamics, identifying the 'boundary layer' and lifting-line theory — and lent his name to a dimensionless number. Who was he?

First isolated in the 1770s and carrying atomic number 25, this hard, silvery transition metal is a key alloying agent in stainless steel and also an essential trace nutrient in the human diet — which element?
Manganese: Chemical element with atomic number 25 (Mn)

First synthesized near Darmstadt in 1982, this fleeting synthetic element — its most stable isotope lasts mere seconds — was named for the Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist Lise Meitner. Which element is it?
Meitnerium: Chemical element with atomic number 109 (Mt)
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.
Native to tropical Central and South America, this genus of 59 flowering plant species belongs to the arum family — which genus?
Nicknamed the 'brain-eating amoeba,' this free-living microorganism lurks in warm freshwater lakes, hot springs, and poorly chlorinated pools — what is it?
A colorless gas with the formula NO, this free radical carries an unpaired electron and can be brewed by lightning in a thunderstorm. What molecule is it?
Nitric oxide: Colorless gas with the formula NO. Nitric oxide (nitrogen oxide, nitrogen mono-oxide, or nitrogen monoxide) is a colorless gas with the formula NO.
First described in 1689 by a local naturalist, this aquatic cave-dwelling salamander is the only exclusively cave-dwelling chordate native to Europe — what is it?
Britain, Germany, and Italy jointly built this twin-engine, variable-sweep-wing combat jet through a tri-national consortium, first flying it in 1974 — which aircraft?
Panavia Tornado: Family of multi-role combat aircraft.

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Brightly colored as a warning sign, these diurnal tropical amphibians of Central and South America brew their toxicity from a diet of ants, mites, and termites — what's this group of frogs?
Poison dart frog: Family of amphibians.

Derived from arachidonic acid and containing a distinctive 5-carbon ring among its 20 carbons, this lipid compound can trigger opposite effects in different body tissues. What hormone-like substance is it?
Prostaglandin: Group of physiologically active lipid compounds.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Also called baked-apple berry or Arctic berry, this amber-hued fruit resembling a blackberry grows wild across boreal forests and Arctic tundra — what's its scientific name?
Rubus chamaemorus: Species of flowering plant in the rose family.
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.

Though crustaceans within this food category are more closely related to insects and spiders than to true fish, what group — including molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms — ranks among the most common food allergens?
Shellfish: Culinary and fisheries term for exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.

This congenital heart defect combines four distinct abnormalities — including a hole between the ventricles and a narrowed pulmonary exit — and can trigger cyanotic 'spells' in infants — what is this condition?
Tetralogy of Fallot: Type of congenital heart defect. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), formerly known as Steno-Fallot tetralogy, is a congenital heart defect characterized by four specific cardiac defects.
This white compound found in sunscreen, paint, and food coloring under the number E171 makes up two-thirds of all pigments used worldwide and is valued at over $13 billion — what is it?
Titanium dioxide: Chemical compound. Titanium dioxide, also known as titanium(IV) oxide or titania, is the inorganic compound derived from titanium with the chemical formula TiO2.

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
